blocks.h2: Is Your Algonquin Water Heater Failing?
blocks.intro: Here's what we hear about most:

tiles.body: A worn thermocouple or flame sensor, usually a quick repair.

tiles.h3: Not Enough Hot Water for the Family
tiles.body: Sediment in the tank, a failing element or a heater that's too small for the household.
Mineral sediment on the bottom of the tank. A flush may help if it's caught early.
From a valve or fitting, it's a repair. From the tank itself, it's time to replace.

blocks.h2: Water Heater Problems in Algonquin Homes
blocks.intro: More than half of Algonquin homes went up between 1990 and 2009. That means a lot of water heaters reaching the end at the same time.

items.h3: The Heater That Came With the House
items.body: A tank heater usually lasts about 8 to 12 years. If yours is original to a home from the 1990s or 2000s, it's well past that. Plan the replacement before it leaks into a finished basement.
Algonquin's water comes from village wells on both sides of the Fox River. Groundwater carries minerals that settle in the tank over time, so yearly flushing matters.
Many homes on well water have water softeners. When a softener runs out of salt or stops regenerating, scale builds in the heater fast. We check it on every water heater call.
Family homes with three or four bathrooms can outgrow a builder-grade 40-gallon tank.

bodies: We work on every residential water heater you'll find in Algonquin: gas and electric tanks, power-vent and high-efficiency models and tankless units. We figure out what's wrong first, then recommend.

The label on the side of your tank lists the fuel, the capacity and the manufacture date, usually hidden in the serial number. Read it to us when you call. If it's time for a new one, see [water heater installation](/algonquin/water-heater-installation).
Well water leaves sediment in every tank. A yearly flush clears it before it hardens, which keeps the heater quieter, more efficient and longer-lasting.

A maintenance visit covers the flush, the relief valve, the anode rod, the burner or elements and the venting. Tankless units get descaled. If you have a softener, we'll make sure it's set for your household.

blocks.h2: Water Heater Questions From Algonquin Homeowners

items.q: My water heater is original to my 1990s house. Should I replace it?
items.preview: Most likely. It's past the typical life of a tank.
items.answer: Most likely. Tank heaters usually last about 8 to 12 years. An original heater from the 1990s or early 2000s is living on borrowed time, and replacing it on your schedule is easier than dealing with a leak.

items.q: Why does my water heater knock?
items.preview: Sediment on the bottom of the tank.
items.answer: Water trapped under sediment boils and knocks as the burner heats it. A flush may quiet it if the sediment hasn't hardened.

items.q: Does a water softener help my water heater?
items.preview: Yes. It cuts the scale that shortens tank life.
items.answer: Yes. Softened water leaves less scale in the tank and on elements. It also makes the anode rod work harder, so we check that during service.

items.q: Is my leaking water heater dangerous?
items.preview: Usually not, but shut it off and call.
items.answer: A leak isn't usually dangerous, but it won't stop. Turn off the cold water valve on top, set a gas heater to pilot or off and call us. If you smell gas, leave and call Nicor Gas or 911 from outside.

items.q: What does water heater repair cost in Algonquin?
items.preview: It depends on the part and the heater. The price comes first.
items.answer: It depends on what failed and the type of heater. We diagnose it and quote a flat rate before we start.
